extracted.intended_audience: news writing instructors and journalism educators
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and using a videotaped mock press conference as a visual-communication teaching event for news-writing students, including format selection, participant roles, question preparation, and post-event evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide exposure and experience covering press conferences
rubrics_metrics.description: A videotape program was designed for use in news writing classes to provide journalism students with exposure to and experience in covering press conferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The primary instructional objective is experiential: give students realistic practice in attending and reporting on press conferences rather than only reading about them in textbooks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select mock press conference format to fill curricular gap
rubrics_metrics.description: The mock press conference format was selected because an analysis of journalism textbooks revealed little attention to this topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose this format when course materials omit substantive coverage of press-conference coverage; select a simulated event to address gaps in the curriculum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a real elected public official as the interviewee
rubrics_metrics.description: It was decided that an elected public official from the San Diego City Council should serve as the interviewee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hiring or inviting an actual public official adds realism and authentic material for students to practice on; select an interviewee relevant to local public affairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Students serve as the press corps
rubrics_metrics.description: Students from a public affairs reporting class should serve as members of the 'press corps.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have enrolled students take on the reporter roles to simulate real press dynamics and give them direct practice; this enables active learning rather than passive observation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include professional journalist and faculty participation
rubrics_metrics.description: A staff writer from the 'San Diego Union' and a broadcast journalism professor also participated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Involve practicing journalists and experienced faculty to model professional standards, provide expert questioning, and offer professional critique and perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure the program with event plus evaluation segment
rubrics_metrics.description: The 33-minute mock press conference ... was followed by an 18-minute evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocate time for both the simulated event and a post-event evaluation/debrief; include an explicit evaluation segment to discuss strengths, weaknesses, and learning points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require researched questions across varied topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Students/reporters asked researched questions over a wide array of topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure student questions are prepared and fact-based and that they cover a range of relevant issues to mirror real press conferences and broaden learning opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicit viewer feedback from multiple classes
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments solicited from students and instructors in three different classes who viewed the videotaped program ... indicated that, overall, the production was a useful educational experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gather qualitative feedback from several classes/instructors who view the program to assess perceived usefulness and instruction value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommend empirical research on program effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Research generating quantitative data regarding the effectiveness of this program as representative of visual communication is called for.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complement qualitative comments with formal quantitative evaluation (e.g., pre/post measures, rubric-based assessments) to validate the program's effectiveness as a teaching tool.
